root_cause.text: In netfilter x_tables native and compat get-entries syscalls, copy_to_user copies the entire rule entry header (including the counters field containing a percpu pointer) to userspace before overwriting it with a sanitized counter snapshot, so a page fault during that initial copy can leave the raw percpu pointer exposed in userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "A caller can provide a userspace buffer that faults during the initial fixed-header copy after pcnt has been copied but before the later sanitized counter copy runs. The syscall then returns -EFAULT while leaving the raw percpu pointer in userspace." The patch changes all affected paths (arp_tables.c, ip_tables.c, ip6_tables.c) to first copy only up to offsetof(entry, counters) and then separately copy the sanitized counters, preventing the percpu pointer from being copied.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential exposure of stale counter data in arptables by not copying the counters field from the entry struct and instead directly writing the correct counters from the separate counters array.
intent_record.what: Merged two separate copy_to_user calls into one combined conditional; the first copy now copies only up to offsetof(struct arpt_entry, counters) instead of sizeof(*e), and the second copy remains unchanged; error handling combined into a single if statement.
intent_record.how: The change avoids writing the counters field from the entry structure to userspace by only copying the fields before counters, then copying the correct counters from the separate counters array, preventing potential exposure of stale or incorrect counter data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix compat copy of arpt_entry by using offsetof of the compat structure to avoid layout mismatch.
intent_record.what: Changed the first copy_to_user size from sizeof(struct arpt_entry) to offsetof(struct compat_arpt_entry, counters) and removed explicit '!= 0' comparisons.
intent_record.how: Ensures that only the part of the native arpt_entry up to the counters field (according to the compat structure layout) is copied, then separately copies the counters. This prevents mismatched sizes and alignment issues between native and compat structures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix copying of ipt_entry to user space by splitting the copy to avoid leaking kernel pointer data from the counters field.
intent_record.what: Combined two copy_to_user calls into one conditional, changing the first to copy only up to offsetof(struct ipt_entry, counters) instead of the entire entry, and keeping the second for counters. The error check now returns -EFAULT if either copy fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the kernel now copies only the non-counters portion of the ipt_entry structure to user space, then copies the actual counter values from the separate counters array, avoiding copying kernel-internal pointers that might be stored in the counters field of the entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix compat ipt_entry copy by using offsetof to correctly handle structure layout differences between native and 32-bit compat modes.
intent_record.what: In the compat_copy_entry_to_user function, the first copy_to_user call now copies only up to the 'counters' field using offsetof(struct compat_ipt_entry, counters) instead of the full sizeof(struct ipt_entry). The explicit comparison to 0 was removed from both copy_to_user calls, relying on non-zero return as error.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when copying an ipt_entry from kernel to user space for compat (32-bit) mode, only the common part of the structure is copied before separately copying the counters. This prevents copying extra or misaligned data due to differences between native and compat structure layouts, fixing potential ABI mismatches and kernel memory leaks. The error check remains effective because copy_to_user returns the number of bytes not copied (non-zero on failure).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential information leak by not exposing kernel counters in the entry copy; copy entry without counters and then write counters separately with combined error checking.
intent_record.what: Modified the copy_entries_to_user function to split the copy of each entry into two parts: first, copy the entry up to but excluding the counters field (using offsetof), then copy the counters from a separate array. The two copy_to_user calls are now combined with logical OR, so that if either fails, the same error handling (jump to free_counters) is executed.
intent_record.how: Previously, the entire entry (including the counters field) was copied first, then the counters were overwritten with the correct values. This could leave kernel-sensitive counters data visible in user space if the second copy failed. Now, the counters field is only written once with the proper user-supplied data, preventing potential information leaks. The combined error handling ensures consistent behavior on failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix compat copy of ip6t_entry to use appropriate compat structure size, preventing overcopy and potential memory corruption in compat entry translation.
intent_record.what: Changed the first copy_to_user in compat_copy_entry_to_user from copying sizeof(struct ip6t_entry) to copying offsetof(struct compat_ip6t_entry, counters), and removed explicit '!= 0' comparisons.
intent_record.how: This ensures that only the compat-sized portion of the entry (up to the counters field) is copied to user space, preventing overcopy and potential data corruption when handling 32-bit compat entries on 64-bit kernels.
